note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Entities Plain, Retained (versioned: { retain: true }) and Unique (unique: { byEmail: ['email'] }) over { id, email?: string, counts: Record<string, number> as SparseMap() field 'sr', codes: Record<string, NumberFromString> as SparseMap(), lists: Record<string, number[]> as SparseMap() field 'sl', objs: Record<string, { n: number, s?: string }> as SparseMap(), texts: Record<string, NumberFromString[]> as SparseMap(), marks: Record<string, { kind: 'raw', value: number } | { kind: 'text', value: string }> as SparseMap(), deep: Record<string, { o?: an annotated Schema.Class { b: number } }> as SparseMap(), held: { n: number > 0, blob: a declared { n: number } } }, on DynamoSchema.make({ name: 'ev', version: 1 }). Each case starts from a row put with counts { a: 1 }, codes { a: 1 }, lists { k: [1] }, objs { k: { n: 1 } }, texts { k: [1] }, marks { a: raw 1, b: text 'x' }, deep { k: { o: { b: 1 } } }, held { n: 1, blob: { n: 1 } } (the renamed maps whole, as sr and sl), or from one holding the renamed maps as entries (put with counts {} and lists {}, then a raw SET counts#a = 1, lists#k = [1] REMOVE sr, sl) or both (the whole put, then a raw SET counts#a = 7, lists#k = [7]), and sends one update with one path operation writing a value into an entry named by its attribute (or into held), standalone or in Transaction.transactWrite. Recorded: the rows and what get read before the update; its outcome (a result, or a failure's tag and the first line of its message); every request it sent, whole and in order; every row of the table after it; and what get read back. The table's name is replaced by <table>, UUIDs by <token> and timestamps by <time>. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
